clue.text: Imagine old favourite catching cold

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former, so old gives EX

indicators.note: catching means the old favourite holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone pictures a former darling coming down with a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to suppose or imagine it will happen, a near synonym.

clue.text: Delight in appearance

definitions.meaning: to delight someone is to enchant or captivate them
an appearance on stage is an arrival or coming in

explanation.surface: Pleasure at being seen.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enchant; as a noun, the act of coming onto the stage, an appearance.

clue.text: Held back a girl working in military HQ

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means held back or confined
G is an abbreviation for girl
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A young woman kept back while employed at army headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon in Virginia is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense.

clue.text: Anglican keeps rodent in chest

indicators.note: keeps means the Anglican holds the rodent inside

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A churchman keeps a rat in a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a wooden box for storage or transport, a kind of chest.

clue.text: Passes on without a risk of illness

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for passes on goes round the rest

parts.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die, so passes on gives DIES
a bet is a risk or wager

explanation.surface: Someone dies without having taken a chance on an illness, a medical-sounding line.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a disease of blood sugar, so it is an example of an illness.

clue.text: Inane film? It is terribly insignificant!

indicators.note: terribly means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A film critic dismisses a silly movie as utterly trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinitesimal means immeasurably small, and so of negligible importance.

clue.text: Beaten up in Rabat in old Roman province

indicators.note: beaten up means the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is assaulted in Morocco's capital, in an ancient Roman province.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia was the Latin name for the Roman province covering most of Britain.

clue.text: Latest result in evaluation

indicators.note: in means the result is placed within the evaluation

parts.note: a try is a test or trial, an evaluation
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: The newest outcome of an assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means in the current fashion, the latest thing.

clue.text: Painter of body of land in the Seychelles

indicators.note: in means the body of land sits inside the Seychelles code

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle registration code for the Seychelles
an isle is a body of land surrounded by water

explanation.surface: An artist paints an island in the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Sisley was an Anglo-French Impressionist landscape painter.

clue.text: Knight wears old clothing in island kingdom

indicators.note: wears means the knight goes inside the clothing, as a body is inside a garment

parts.note: the toga was the garment of ancient Rome
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight dresses in antique robes on a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian monarchy in the South Pacific, a kingdom made of islands.

clue.text: Distension of birds grasping opponents

indicators.note: grasping means the birds hold the next letters within them

parts.note: puffins are seabirds with bright beaks
E and S, East and South, are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Seabirds clutching their rivals end up bloated.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge East-West play North-South, so any East and South pair are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffiness is swelling, the state of being distended or bloated.

clue.text: Hold down cards and pick up special scissors

parts.note: to pin is to hold down
kings are playing cards
to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: Pinning down a hand of cards and gathering them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinking shears are scissors with serrated blades that cut a zigzag edge to stop fabric fraying.

clue.text: Bold maiden interrupts unnamed Greek king

indicators.note: interrupts means the bold maiden breaks into the word for unnamed

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, means unnamed
game means plucky or bold, as in game for anything
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A brave young woman cuts in on a nameless Greek ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Confuse designated driver tucking into alcoholic drink

indicators.note: tucking into means the driver goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: The sober driver drinking beer would muddle things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like eating, but it signals putting one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle or befuddle, a synonym for confuse.

clue.text: Meet behind bar when tight

indicators.note: behind means the word for meet comes after the word for bar

parts.note: to bar a door is to close it
meet in its old sense means proper or fitting

explanation.surface: Getting together at the back of a pub while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like slang for drunk; it is the definition in its sense of snug.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting garment sits snugly against the body, so it is tight.

clue.text: Let enamel fuse! That's basic

indicators.note: fuse means the letters melt together into a new form

explanation.surface: A potter lets the glaze melt: that is fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental, relating to first principles, hence basic.

clue.text: Claim for oneself Yorkshire town lacks aspiration

indicators.note: lacks means the town goes without the sound of breath

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire
aspiration is the breathy sound of the letter H

explanation.surface: A northern town is said to have no ambition, but claims otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition, but it is the phonetic term for an H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to take or claim something without justification for oneself.

clue.text: Turn in the troika is done

indicators.note: in means the turn goes inside the sledge

parts.note: a troika is a Russian sledge drawn by three horses, so it gives SLED
to wind is to turn, as a key or a road

explanation.surface: A turn in the three-horse sleigh is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Being done is slang for being cheated, the same as being swindled.

clue.text: Winger prevaricates even before disagreement

indicators.note: before means the earlier pieces come ahead of the word for disagreement

parts.note: to hedge is to avoid committing oneself, to prevaricate
par means even, as in on a par
a row is a quarrel or disagreement

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing dodges the question just ahead of a bust-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer; here it is something with wings, a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedge sparrow, or dunnock, is a small bird, and a winger in crossword terms is anything that flies.

clue.text: Emergencies? Charlie does his best!

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
someone who does his best rises to the occasion

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie copes well when things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are moments of danger or difficulty that demand action, emergencies.

clue.text: Royalist leaders capture commanders in style

indicators.note: leaders means the opening letters of the word Royalist

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer, so two commanders give two of them

explanation.surface: Cavalier leaders seize officers in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first two letters of 'Royalist'; 'capture' only joins them to the two commanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century style of art and architecture.

clue.text: Heron played in the river

indicators.note: played means the letters of the bird are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A heron frolics in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river running from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: When groom transformed native

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of the two words are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bridegroom changes and turns local.
explanation.definitionFit: Home-grown means produced locally rather than imported, so native to a place.

clue.text: Some bring us together for exhilaration

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Uniting us gives a sense of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for exhilaration' as the definition, but 'for' is a link word: the answer means exhilaration, not 'for exhilaration'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and zest, close in sense to exhilaration.

clue.text: Deficiency in squat, leading to collapse

indicators.note: leading to means the word for squat comes first, followed by the word for collapse

parts.note: squat means short and stocky
a fall is a collapse

explanation.surface: A shortage in a crouching exercise ends with someone toppling over.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is an amount by which something falls short, a deficit.

clue.text: Old Bob's lofty hedge

parts.note: a bob was slang for the old British shilling, abbreviated s; the 's here means has
lofty means tall

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Bob has a towering hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling, or bob, was a pre-decimal British coin worth twelve pence; its abbreviation was s.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge and to stall are both to avoid giving a straight answer, to play for time.

clue.text: Notice the French head of state is immaculate

parts.note: to spot is to notice
les is French for the (plural)

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word state

explanation.surface: Observe that the French president is beyond reproach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' reads as a leader, but only 'head of' is an indicator, taking the first letter of 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means without a mark or blemish, the same as immaculate.

clue.text: Be inclined to keep work of the highest quality

indicators.note: to keep means the word for be inclined holds the work inside it

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be inclined to
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone is disposed to keep a first-rate piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-end goods are at the upper end of the market, the best quality available.
